verdict.rationale: The open-source Ramp CLI is documented for unattended use. `--no-input` disables prompts for CI, `--agent` emits JSON for scripting, standalone agents authenticate without a browser via OAuth client credentials (RAMP_CLIENT_ID/RAMP_CLIENT_SECRET), and RAMP_PROFILE pins an identity for automation. The AI Agents guide names the CLI as the channel for scripted and scheduled workflows, and the API supports client-credentials server-to-server auth. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the CLI running in an actual CI pipeline (no CI-specific example such as a GitHub Actions setup).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Standalone agents authenticate without a browser by exchanging OAuth client credentials for a production access token
RAMP_PROFILE pins an identity for automation.
Coding agents (or any agent with terminal access) and scripted/scheduled workflows
The CLI outputs JSON in agent mode and is built for scripted loops
